weeks.headline: Messaging, remade
weeks.dek: Photos you can mark up, voice notes that look like a radio intercept, and stickers that finally feel like messages. On every platform at once.

items.title: Edit a photo before you send it
items.body: Crop, draw, add text and stickers, write a caption. Change your mind and re-open the edit before it goes.

items.title: Full-screen photos that zoom
items.body: Tap any photo in a chat. Pinch, double-tap, scroll the wheel, pan around.

items.title: Voice notes, as a thermal readout
items.body: Record right inside the text field. The waveform follows your real voice, and sent notes play back like a radio pickup.

items.title: Stickers and GIFs, one tap away
items.body: They send as their own messages, and the picker stays open so you can send a few in a row.

items.title: A camera-first + button
items.body: The + opens our own half sheet: camera up top, then photos, files, location.

items.title: Find anyone on Jokuh
items.body: New Call and Find people now search everyone, not just the people you already know.

weeks.headline: Walkie-talkie, Fuel, and the week ahead
weeks.dek: Our busiest week yet: voice messages you hold to talk, an Arcade that runs on its own token, and a Spine that knows what's on near you.

items.title: Walkie-talkie voice messages
items.body: Tap to record hands-free, or hold to talk and let go to send. With a little splat when it lands.

items.title: Shared Spine, inside the chat
items.body: Open a conversation and see the year you two have had: calls, photos, plans, all in one lane.

items.title: Events you're going to, and ones nearby
items.body: Your RSVPs show up as rich Going rows, with suggestions for what's on around you. Hours with an event glow Jokuh orange.

items.title: The Arcade runs on Fuel
items.body: Tickets, payouts and prizes all run on Fuel, the Arcade's own token. Everyday games stay free.

items.title: Tip with Batcoin, hold your own Zcash
items.body: Tip people across the app, and keep Zcash in a wallet only you hold the keys to.

items.title: Chats open instantly, even offline
items.body: Your history paints from the device the moment you open a chat, signal or not.

weeks.headline: Gooey, for everyone
weeks.dek: One look across every screen, calls that connect the first time, and a Mac palette that finds anything.

items.title: Gooey is the new look
items.body: Glassy chrome, Satoshi type, and Gooey Light and Dark themes, on by default for everyone.

items.title: Real squircles, everywhere
items.body: Every container uses the same fully smoothed corner as our Figma files. You feel it more than you see it.

items.title: Calls that just connect
items.body: Audio that doesn't drop out, 1080p video, and one control dock instead of three.

items.title: Connect your apps in one tap
items.body: Link the apps you use, and OO can work with them inside your DMs and huddles.

items.title: A palette that finds anything
items.body: Memories, chats, people, sites you've visited, a world clock and unit conversions, a keystroke away.

items.title: Your space
items.body: Your own blurbs orbit your profile, and the pod turns into a composer while it's open.

weeks.headline: A calmer Jokuh
weeks.dek: We took things away this week. The core app gets quieter, and the extras wait until you ask for them.

items.title: Extra tools, off until you want them
items.body: The experimental stuff now lives behind one switch in Settings. Out of the box you get calls, texts, Spine and your profile.

items.title: Calls and DMs show the essentials
items.body: Beta buttons and message actions move behind the same switch, so the everyday screens stay clean.

items.title: Less work in the background
items.body: The web app skips the heavy background work until you need it.

weeks.headline: Under the hood
weeks.dek: A quiet week on the surface. Underneath, we tightened the walls around your account.

items.title: Stronger account boundaries
items.body: A full pass over sign-in, database access rules and our service gateway.

items.title: Recovers when things go wrong
items.body: New crash and timeout recovery, so a bad network moment doesn't take the app down with it.

items.title: A cleaner wallet
items.body: A new wallet header and simpler token rows.

weeks.headline: Blurbs on your profile
weeks.dek: Your blurbs get a home on your ID, and OO learns to look after the people and pets in your life.

items.title: A Blurbs pod for your profile
items.body: A chat-bubble thumbnail with little floaters, and a sheet with your latest blurbs.

items.title: A rainbow identity
items.body: Blurbs gets its own dark-rainbow look, with a bit of game to it.

items.title: Pet care, partners and a daily check-in
items.body: OO can help with pet care, there's a new bond for partners, and Spine asks how your day went.

items.title: Months open where you stop
items.body: Scroll Spine and the month you settle on opens by itself.

weeks.headline: Build your profile from pods
weeks.dek: Your ID becomes a set of pods you pick and arrange: music, gallery, location, about. And claiming your handle now comes with confetti.

items.title: Profile pods
items.body: Add music, a gallery, where you are, your story, and lay them out the way you like.

items.title: About, expanded
items.body: Tap About to open your whole story, on your own profile and on public ones.

items.title: Claim your @handle, with confetti
items.body: Pick your handle and it bursts. If it's taken, you see who has it.

items.title: A first-blurb reward
items.body: New people get a reward for their first blurb, and topics picked for them from what they like.

items.title: Today, sandwiched
items.body: Past hours sit above the now pill, and what's coming sits below.

weeks.headline: Sealed
weeks.dek: Messages go end-to-end encrypted. DMs, huddles and in-call chat are sealed on every platform, and we can't read them.

items.title: End-to-end encrypted messaging
items.body: DMs, huddles and chat inside calls are sealed on your device before they leave it.

items.title: Translation only with consent
items.body: On sealed calls, live translation only runs when everyone in the call agrees.

items.title: The Arcade gets its own chain
items.body: An Avalanche L1 for the Arcade, the groundwork for what later became Fuel.

items.title: Your living week
items.body: Spine keeps a rolling picture of your week, on every platform.

weeks.headline: Lighter and faster
weeks.dek: A full-stack speed pass: smaller downloads, a quicker database, and live updates instead of constant checking.

items.title: A smaller, faster app
items.body: We cut the app's download size and sped up the database behind it.

items.title: Calls update live
items.body: Pulse uses realtime updates instead of asking the server every few seconds.

items.title: Bubbles opens in a snap
items.body: The Bubbles drawer opens and scrolls faster, even with long histories.

items.title: Delete your account from the app
items.body: One place in Settings, no email required.

weeks.headline: Blocks, widgets and GIFs
weeks.dek: Answers come back as cards, Jokuh lands on your Home Screen, and chats get GIFs and mentions.

items.title: Cortex Blocks
items.body: Answers come back as cards, lists and comparisons you can scan, not walls of text.

items.title: Home Screen widgets
items.body: A set of Jokuh widgets, so the day's brief is one glance away.

items.title: GIFs, mentions and attachments
items.body: A GIF picker, @mentions and richer attachments in every chat.

items.title: Today Brief chips
items.body: Quick chips at the top of Spine for what matters today, with a few new sounds.

items.title: More Arcade
items.body: More games to play inside Jokuh.

weeks.headline: Meet Cortex
weeks.dek: An AI you can chat with that knows your Spine, a look at the sky, and Jokuh in more languages.

items.title: Cortex chat
items.body: Ask anything, and get answers grounded in your own memories.

items.title: Sky lens
items.body: What's happening overhead, right inside your day.

items.title: More languages
items.body: A big translation wave across the app.

items.title: Your devices stay in sync
items.body: Start on your phone, pick it up on your Mac.

weeks.headline: Share anything into Spine
weeks.dek: Send a link, a photo or a note from any app and Jokuh asks where it belongs.

items.title: Share to Spine
items.body: Use the share sheet from any app. Save it to Spine, or turn it into a text or a blurb.

items.title: A daily brief and photo moments
items.body: Open Jokuh to a short brief of your day, with your best photos pulled forward.

items.title: A soundboard
items.body: Drop a sound into the call.

items.title: Dark paper
items.body: Sheets get a dark paper texture, and Nexus learns timers and toasts.

weeks.headline: A wallet, and OO calls you back
weeks.dek: The first wallet, OO that phones you when it has an answer, and an OO that can use your other apps.

items.title: The first wallet
items.body: See and move what you hold, right inside Jokuh.

items.title: OO calls you back
items.body: Ask OO something that takes a while, and it calls you when it's done.

items.title: OO uses your apps
items.body: Connect services and OO can take real steps with them, not just talk.

items.title: Smoother live streams
items.body: Profile Live moves to a new streaming backbone, plus Beam rooms.

items.title: Faster launch
items.body: We measured cold launch and took the congestion out of it.

weeks.headline: Go live
weeks.dek: Broadcast from your profile, let people book time with you, and meet the agents who liven up Blurbs.

items.title: Profile Live
items.body: Go live from your profile. On iPhone you can broadcast your screen too.

items.title: Book time with me
items.body: Share a public Spine link and people can pick a slot. Meeting invites arrive by email with an RSVP.

items.title: Agents that react
items.body: AI characters show up on Blurbs, react to posts, and remember the conversation.

items.title: Studio
items.body: Make images without leaving Jokuh.

items.title: Tell us what's off
items.body: An in-app feedback inbox that goes straight to the team.

weeks.headline: Meetings on the calendar
weeks.dek: One big drop: schedule a call ahead of time, and huddles on every platform.

items.title: Scheduled meetings
items.body: Put a Pulse call on the calendar and everyone gets the link.

items.title: Huddles, everywhere
items.body: Drop-in group voice works the same on phone, Mac and web.

weeks.headline: The Arcade opens
weeks.dek: Games inside Jokuh, a voice agent you can just talk to, and calls that translate as you speak.

items.title: The Arcade
items.body: Games you can play with friends, right in the app.

items.title: A realtime voice agent
items.body: Talk out loud and get an answer back in real time.

items.title: Live call translation
items.body: Speak your language and they hear theirs.

items.title: Dark app icons
items.body: Jokuh matches your Home Screen in dark mode.

weeks.headline: Bubbles and huddles
weeks.dek: Small group spaces with a voice room built in, and a place in Spine for your files.

items.title: Bubbles and huddles
items.body: A space for your group, with a huddle you can drop into any time.

items.title: A file library
items.body: Files you share and save, organised in Spine.

items.title: Search and calls, more reliable
items.body: Better search results, and fewer calls that fail to connect.

weeks.headline: Your Daily Pulse
weeks.dek: Spine starts the day with you, and everything gets a little snappier.

items.title: Spine Daily Pulse
items.body: A personal read of your day, written for you each morning.

items.title: Paste to send
items.body: Paste an image straight into a DM, and send photos without typing anything.

items.title: Formatting and sources in bubbles
items.body: Bold, lists and links render inside messages, and answers show their sources.

items.title: Snappier by feel
items.body: Sheets react the instant you touch them, pills tap back with haptics, and animations got a tighter budget.

weeks.headline: Speed week
weeks.dek: We load-tested everything and fixed what we found. Plus a browser built for your thumb.

items.title: Faster everywhere
items.body: Images load ahead of you, skeletons replace spinners, and Spine opens without waiting.

items.title: A browser for your thumb
items.body: The in-app browser goes full width, with tabs as dots under the address bar.

items.title: Search that knows what you mean
items.body: Type a command and it runs. Type anything else and you get the web.

items.title: Push notifications
items.body: Messages and calls reach you when the app is closed.

weeks.headline: Blurbs arrive
weeks.dek: A social feed of your own, group chats, reactions, and the first Android build.

items.title: Blurbs
items.body: Post short thoughts to a feed, each with its own public link you can share anywhere.

items.title: Groups, reactions and Joki packs
items.body: Group threads, a shared planner, reactions, and our own sticker packs.

items.title: Calling, rebuilt
items.body: Clearer audio, group calls, deep links into a call, and transcripts.

items.title: Hello, Android
items.body: The first Android build of Jokuh.

weeks.headline: It's called Jokuh
weeks.dek: The app gets its name, and in one week learns to text, call, and remember.

items.title: Sign in with a passkey
items.body: No passwords. Your face or fingerprint is the key.

items.title: Texts and voice memos
items.body: Messaging with voice memos, attachments and link previews.

items.title: Pulse calls
items.body: Voice and video calls, with our own ringtones and a branded incoming-call screen.

items.title: Calls become memories
items.body: A call's transcript can land in Spine, with privacy controls for what gets kept.

weeks.headline: Starting over, natively
weeks.dek: Most of the week went into agents you can create yourself, richer meetings and a Mac download page. Then on Sunday we started over, building a new native app for iPhone and Mac with a matching web version.

items.title: A fresh native app for iPhone and Mac
items.body: On Sunday we started over, natively. The first build already has the floating island, Spine's year timeline, messages, calls, a built-in browser and your ID page, plus a matching web version.

items.title: Capture moments into Spine
items.body: In the new app you can capture a moment into Spine and preview it before it's saved. A command sheet puts quick actions one tap away.

items.title: Create your own agent
items.body: Type /create agent anywhere, give it a name and a personality, and decide what it can do, like posting blurbs, making images or messaging you with updates.

items.title: Work together during a meeting
items.body: Meetings get a live transcript panel, a shared pad, sticky notes, a soundboard and recording.

items.title: Download Jokuh for Mac
items.body: A new download page gets you the signed Mac app straight from the web.

weeks.headline: Meetings that remember
weeks.dek: Meetings got live captions, transcripts that survive a reload, and summaries that hold up on long calls. OO learned to play media in its replies, and Realms put your spaces on a map.

items.title: Follow a meeting with live captions
items.body: Captions keep running through the whole call, and they no longer make up words while nobody is talking.

items.title: Meeting summaries in your Spine
items.body: Transcripts survive a reload or a rejoin, summaries cover calls that run for hours, and each one is saved to your Spine.

items.title: Push-to-talk and noise reduction
items.body: Hold a key to talk, or turn on noise reduction and echo cancellation. When someone shares their screen, you can zoom in.

items.title: Make audio and video in Studio
items.body: Generate audio and video, with a film strip that keeps everything you've made in order.

items.title: All your spaces on one map
items.body: Realms lays out your spaces on a hexagon map, with its own sounds and a panel for running each space.

items.title: Music and media inside OO's replies
items.body: OO can find or make media and play music right in the chat. Short tips on your first visit replace the old guided tours.

weeks.headline: Search that opens things
weeks.dek: Type what you want and press Enter. Search learned to find and open your services, meetings started following you around the app, and uploads got faster.

items.title: Open a service by typing its name
items.body: Search finds services even with a typo, puts the ones you've connected first, and opens the top result when you press Enter.

items.title: Connect services without leaving Jokuh
items.body: Signing in to a service happens in Jokuh's own browser, and connected services show up as quick picks when you add a link pod to your profile.

items.title: Keep a meeting going as you move around
items.body: A meeting stays in the floating island while you use the rest of the app, and meeting links now point to jokuh.com.

items.title: Faster photo and video uploads
items.body: Photos and videos are compressed and sent in parallel, which makes uploads about 40% faster.

items.title: The first AI agents on Jokuh
items.body: The first AI agents joined as real accounts. Within set rules, they can send messages, make connections, post blurbs and update their profiles.

weeks.headline: Calls that ring, email beside chats
weeks.dek: A week on the everyday basics. Calls ring properly on iPhone, email sits next to your messages, and OO can join your group chats.

items.title: Jokuh calls on your iPhone's call screen
items.body: Incoming Jokuh calls use the iPhone's own call screen, so they ring like a phone call even when the app is closed.

items.title: Send, reply to and forward email
items.body: Email threads sit next to your messages. Reply in the thread, forward messages, and see which address you're sending from.

items.title: Mention @oo in a group chat
items.body: Type @oo in any group to bring OO into the conversation. If several people ask at once, OO answers each in turn.

items.title: See which day each message was sent
items.body: Chats get Today, Yesterday and weekday dividers, and work with screen readers. On iPhone, the keyboard no longer pushes the chat off screen.

items.title: Fill a company profile from its website
items.body: On a company or group profile, enter a web address and Jokuh adds its links, quotes and a short bio for you.

weeks.label: February 2026
weeks.headline: Briefings, Gooey, and a 4K camera
weeks.dek: OO learned to catch you up on what you missed, and Spine started looking back at your past. Blurbs got a much better camera, and the Gooey look took shape.

items.title: Catch up with an OO briefing
items.body: Come back and OO greets you with a short briefing. A daily or weekly summary gathers your to-dos, highlights and messages, with suggested replies you can send in one tap.

items.title: Look back with On This Day
items.body: Spine marks holidays and brings back what happened on this day in past years. Emails and scheduled meetings show up as memories too.

items.title: Writing help in your notes
items.body: Notes suggest the next words as you type, and can draw a diagram or find an inspiration image from what you've written.

items.title: Shoot Blurbs in up to 4K
items.body: The Blurbs camera records up to 4K with sound, with tap to focus and exposure. One Blurb can hold several photos or videos.

items.title: Quick replies and 3,000 emoji
items.body: Chats suggest quick replies, and the emoji picker has more than 3,000 emoji.

items.title: Meet Gooey
items.body: We built Gooey, Jokuh's own set of buttons, cards, chat bubbles and animated icons, and started moving the app over to it.

weeks.label: January 2026
weeks.headline: A timeline, transcripts, and speed
weeks.dek: Spine got a real timeline, calls started writing their own notes, and messaging picked up the gestures you'd expect. We also took out slow animations so the whole app responds right away.

items.title: Place memories on your day's timeline
items.body: Spine shows a 24-hour timeline, and you can drag a memory to the hour it belongs to. Notes, tasks, reminders and meetings open in their own sheets.

items.title: A transcript when the call ends
items.body: When you hang up you get the full transcript and a short summary, saved to Spine for everyone on the call. Voice channels join you as soon as you open them.

items.title: Swipe to reply, preview files in the chat
items.body: Swipe a message to reply, react from a bigger set of emoji and stickers, and search inside a conversation. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files open right in the chat.

items.title: Comment on and share Blurbs
items.body: Blurbs get comments and a share sheet, and new posts appear at the top of the feed without a refresh. Each Blurb stays up for 80 hours.

items.title: Ask the assistant to start a call
items.body: Say "call @username" and the assistant places the call. It can also answer with a map and directions.

items.title: Everything responds right away
items.body: We took out slow animations and heavy blur across the app, so lists, dialogs and replies show up the moment you tap.

weeks.label: December 2025
weeks.headline: Real calls, a wallet, and Blurbs
weeks.dek: We rebuilt voice and video calls to work like a phone, and built a wallet for sending and receiving. Chats got voice notes and stickers, and Blurbs got comments.

items.title: Calls that behave like a phone
items.body: Calls move through clear stages, from calling and ringing to connected, with a dial tone, ringtone and timer. Answer from the lock screen, share your screen, and see when a call was picked up on another device.

items.title: Voice notes, stickers and reactions
items.body: Hold to record a voice note that sends with its waveform. React with emoji, send animated stickers, and share your location in a chat.

items.title: Send and receive from your wallet
items.body: Send to a friend by name or to an address, and receive with a QR code, on several networks. An Activity tab lists what came in and went out.

items.title: Your calendar and payments on Spine
items.body: Connect Google, Outlook or Apple calendars and your events show up on Spine. Money you send or receive is saved as a memory on that day.

items.title: Comment and reply on Blurbs
items.body: Blurbs take comments with likes and threaded replies. Posting got pinch-to-zoom, camera flip and saved drafts.

items.title: Chats open faster, even offline
items.body: Your profile and chats load from what's already on your device, so screens appear right away. Long conversations scroll smoothly instead of freezing.

weeks.label: November 2025
weeks.headline: Lock-screen calls, roles, and reminders
weeks.dek: Calls started ringing like real phone calls, and chats picked up the basics people expect. Group spaces got roles and categories, and Spine learned to remind you of things.

items.title: Answer calls from your lock screen
items.body: On phones, incoming calls ring like a normal phone call, and tapping a notification opens the right chat. On desktop, a simpler call window tells you when a call was declined, missed or busy.

items.title: Send any file, and never lose a draft
items.body: Chats take photos, videos, audio and documents, with previews for links you paste. Unsent drafts stay put when you leave a chat, and you can see when someone is typing.

items.title: Roles and categories for group spaces
items.body: Give members roles that decide which channels they see, group channels into categories, and color-code them. Share an invite link and new people join as soon as they sign in.

items.title: Set reminders right on your Spine
items.body: Pick a time on any day and Spine reminds you when it arrives. The timeline opens on today, and busy days show every memory at a glance.

items.title: Control what's playing from Nexus
items.body: Nexus in the desktop app works as a media player, with play and pause, seeking, volume and speed. It remembers where you left off.

items.title: More games in the Arcade
items.body: The Arcade added 2048, chess, solitaire, FreeCell, Minesweeper and a side-scrolling platformer.

weeks.label: October 2025
weeks.headline: Messages, calls, and group spaces
weeks.dek: Our busiest month at the time: private messages, calls that ring, and group spaces with voice channels. The app started running in a web browser, and we began work on an iPhone version.

items.title: Start a group space with voice channels
items.body: Create a space with a picture, invite people, and see who's a member. Each space gets a voice channel that shows who's speaking and who's muted.

items.title: Message people privately
items.body: Connecting with someone opens a private conversation. Send photos and files, see when your message has been seen, and spot unread chats by their red dot.

items.title: Call someone and hear it ring
items.body: Place an audio or video call to a contact and it rings in Nexus. Missed calls get their own list and a dot on the phone button.

items.title: A brighter, clearer Spine
items.body: Days light up only when they hold memories, and busy days grow wider. Delete a memory, and follow the red line back to today.

items.title: Tetris, Snake, Pong and Breakout
items.body: The first Arcade has four classic games. Type "play" and a game's name, or ask the assistant to open one.

items.title: Jokuh in your browser, and on iPhone
items.body: The app installs from a web browser and has a screen for when you're offline. We also wrapped it for iPhone, edge to edge, with haptics as you tap.

weeks.label: September 2025
weeks.headline: An assistant, video rooms, and Nexus
weeks.dek: September brought an AI assistant into the desktop app, along with the first video rooms and the Nexus island at the top of the screen. Profiles got pods in every size and a page at your own username.

items.title: Chat with an AI assistant
items.body: An assistant chat with a list of past conversations. Pick a model or leave it on Auto, rename a chat with a double-click, and favorite the ones you want to keep.

items.title: Answers with math, diagrams and formatting
items.body: Replies can include formatted text, math and diagrams, and chats title themselves.

items.title: Send photos and ask about the weather
items.body: Attach photos to a chat. The assistant can check the weather where you are, show visual cards, and search the web for images.

items.title: Video rooms that tuck into Nexus
items.body: Start a video room and share its link. Leave the room screen and the call shrinks into Nexus, the floating island at the top, so you can keep working.

items.title: Pods in every size, at your own address
items.body: Image, link, music, quote and profile pods were redesigned for every size and now save between visits. Every profile gets its own page at its username.

items.title: Find people and connect
items.body: Search for someone by name and send a connection request, right from the phone screen.

weeks.label: Summer 2025
weeks.headline: A fresh start on the desktop
weeks.dek: In June we started a new desktop app for Jokuh. Over the summer it got Spine, a profile made of pods, and the Jokuh name.

items.title: Save memories on a day-by-day timeline
items.body: Spine came to the new app: days shown as capsules you can open to save and revisit memories, with a keyboard shortcut sheet and a short welcome tour.

items.title: Build your profile out of pods
items.body: Your ID page became a grid of pods you can resize and arrange, starting with a profile pod for your name and bio, and a music pod.

items.title: Format messages and drop in documents
items.body: Messages show headings, lists, quotes, bold and links in rounded bubbles. Drop in a PDF or photo and the message box reads the text out of it.

items.title: Named Jokuh, with a dark mode
items.body: In July the new app took on the Jokuh name. It follows your light or dark setting from the moment it opens, with no white flash.
